I farm the same 4.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, so I will put all 4.1 mu into wheat first and then all 4.1 mu into maize after wheat harvest. I do not like making big changes at my age. I usually start from what worked last year, then adjust a little if fertilizer price or weather looks different. With only 4.1 mu, every bag costs money, but I still would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose grain. We have well water, so I will not let the crop sit dry if the season turns hard. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put the base fertilizer on a bit heavier, and water around the key stages. Wheat in our area eats fertilizer and water if I want steady ears. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed like most people around here, because the hybrids fill better and yield more if water keeps up. I will keep phosphorus and potassium in, but nitrogen will still be the main thing. I will spray when I need to, not for show, usually once or twice if weeds or insects come up. Tillage-wise, I will use rotary tillage because it fits my small land, my labor, and the way people around me manage stubble. I will aim for a steady harvest, not gamble on cutting inputs too far.
